solution: $\cos^{2}\dfrac{k\pi}{3}$ is $1$ if $3\mid k$ and $\dfrac{1}{4}$ otherwise, so the sum is $A+\dfrac{1}{4}(2^{14}-A)$ with $A=\displaystyle\sum_{3\mid k}\binom{14}{k}$
Multisection with the cube roots of unity $1,\omega,\omega^{2}$: $A=\dfrac{2^{14}+(1+\omega)^{14}+(1+\omega^{2})^{14}}{3}$
solution_full: For integer $k$, $\cos\dfrac{k\pi}{3}\in\left\{\pm1,\pm\dfrac{1}{2}\right\}$: it is $\pm1$ exactly when $3\mid k$. So $\cos^{2}\dfrac{k\pi}{3}=1$ if $3\mid k$ and $\dfrac{1}{4}$ otherwise.
Let $\omega=e^{2\pi i/3}$. Since $1+\omega^{k}+\omega^{2k}$ is $3$ for $3\mid k$ and $0$ otherwise, $3A=2^{14}+(1+\omega)^{14}+(1+\omega^{2})^{14}$.
$1+\omega=e^{i\pi/3}$ and $1+\omega^{2}=e^{-i\pi/3}$ are sixth roots of unity, so $(1+\omega)^{14}+(1+\omega^{2})^{14}=2\cos\dfrac{14\pi}{3}=2\cos\dfrac{2\pi}{3}=-1$.
originality_note: New: the weight cos^2(k pi/3) takes only the values 1 and 1/4, so the sum is a weighted multisection of the binomial row (way 4). Closest known: sums C(n,0)+C(n,3)+C(n,6)+... and sum C(n,k) cos k theta = Re(1+e^{i theta})^n. Different because: the square of the cosine is used as the weight, which the student must recognise as a two-valued filter or reduce by the double angle.
blueprint_concepts: Multisection of series using roots of unity

concept_use.nth root of unity: 1+omega = e^{i pi/3} is a sixth root of unity, so its 14th power is e^{14 i pi/3} = e^{2 i pi/3}.
concept_use.Multisection of series using roots of un: A = sum of C(14,3k) is extracted with the filter 1+omega^k+omega^{2k}, and the cos^2 weight splits the row into multiples of 3 and the rest.

key_step: See cos^2(k pi/3) as 1 or 1/4 and extract the multiples of 3 by the cube-root filter.
justification: One standard filter plus a weighting observation; routine chain, numerical. Level 2, like 2023-P1-Q13 (L1) raised by the extra multisection step.
